findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with empty data when feature flag is enabled
findings.body: When the feature flag `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{ data: [], meta: { fields: {}, units: {} } }} />` with hardcoded empty data, completely ignoring the computed `tableResults` and `result` variables that contain the actual table data. Any organization with this feature flag enabled will see empty tables in their dashboard widgets instead of the actual query data. The component should receive the real `tableResults` data (likely mapped to the `TabularData` format that `TableWidgetVisualization` expects).

findings.title: Default autofix automation tuning silently changed from 'low' to 'off'
findings.body: `DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT` was changed from `"low"` to `"off"` without any indication in the PR description. This changes the default behavior for new projects: autofix will no longer run automatically on new issues by default. The corresponding project option default in `src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py` (line 205) was also changed. This is a user-facing behavior change that should be called out explicitly in the PR description and potentially coordinated with documentation/release notes, as existing projects that rely on the default will not be affected, but new projects will have a different experience.

findings.title: Analytics recorded before feature flag check
findings.body: The `analytics.record(...)` call for `preprod_artifact.api.assemble` is placed before the `features.has(...)` check. This means analytics events are recorded for every request to this endpoint, including requests from organizations where the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature is disabled (which return 404). This inflates analytics metrics with requests from users who can't actually use the feature. If the intent is to track actual usage, the analytics call should be moved after the feature flag check.

findings.title: dcg_to_slow_conditions source changed from dcg_to_groups.keys() to dcg_ids
findings.body: Previously, `get_condition_query_groups` computed `dcg_to_slow_conditions` from `list(event_data.dcg_to_groups.keys())`, while `get_groups_to_fire` computed it from `list(event_data.dcg_ids)`. The refactoring unifies both to use `list(event_data.dcg_ids)` (computed once in `process_delayed_workflows`). If `event_data.dcg_ids` and `event_data.dcg_to_groups.keys()` contain different sets of DCG IDs, this changes which DCGs have their slow conditions fetched and could alter workflow firing behavior. The behavioral difference should be verified and tests should cover the case where these two sets differ.

findings.title: Broad except in get_environment_info swallows all errors silently
findings.body: `get_environment_info` catches a bare `Exception` and only logs at info level via `logger.info(...)`. This swallows all errors including programming errors (AttributeError, TypeError, etc.) silently, making debugging difficult. The intent seems to be to gracefully handle cases where the environment can't be determined, but catching all exceptions is too broad. At minimum, the exception type should be narrowed (e.g., `Event.DoesNotExist`, `NodeData.DoesNotExist`) or the bare except should log at warning/error level for unexpected exceptions.

findings.title: Feedback separator changed from list format to raw join
findings.body:
The separator for joining feedback entries changed from `"
".join(f"- {msg}" for msg in feedbacks)` (which produced a bulleted list) to `"
------
".join(feedbacks)` (which produces raw separator-delimited entries). This is a significant change in how feedback is presented to the LLM. If any feedback message contains the substring `------`, it could be confused with a separator. Additionally, the new format doesn't provide visual structure (no bullet points), which may affect LLM summarization quality. This should be tested to ensure the LLM still produces good summaries with the new format.
